issues.title: Logic inversion in hasPendingInviteByUserId method
issues.description: The hasPendingInviteByUserId method checks for accepted:true memberships instead of accepted:false (pending invites). This inverts the method's logic - it will return true when users have accepted team memberships rather than pending invites. This breaks the onboarding flow for users with team invites, causing users with accepted memberships to be redirected to personal onboarding instead of users with pending invites. The method name and its intended purpose clearly indicate it should check for pending (non-accepted) invites.

issues.title: Incorrect conditional operator in onboarding redirect logic
issues.description: The conditional logic for redirecting users with pending invites uses OR (||) instead of AND (&&). This means users will be redirected to '/onboarding/personal/settings' if they have a pending invite OR if onboarding-v3 is enabled, rather than requiring both conditions. This breaks the normal onboarding flow - any user with onboarding-v3 enabled will be incorrectly redirected to personal settings regardless of whether they have pending invites. The intended behavior was to only redirect users who have both onboarding-v3 enabled AND a pending invite.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #26829 - fix: add server-side redirect for users with pending invites on onboarding page

structured_output.summary:
The PR tries to stop users who signed up through a team invite from landing on the plan-selection page at /onboarding/getting-started. It adds a static MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId helper, uses it to redirect from the getting-started server page to /onboarding/personal/settings, and swaps a direct prisma.membership query in onboardingUtils.checkOnboardingRedirect for the same helper. It also adds integration tests for the helper.

The intent is reasonable, but the implementation has a blocking defect. The helper's name and the PR description both say it should look for pending invites (accepted: false), yet the query filters on accepted: true. That returns true for any user who is already a member of a team, so the check is inverted. On top of that, the onboardingUtils condition changed from `&&` to `||`, which sends every user to personal onboarding whenever the onboarding-v3 flag is on. The integration tests were written against the intended semantics, so they fail against the code as written.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The helper queries accepted: true while its name and the PR description say it should find pending invites (accepted: false). As written, the getting-started redirect fires for existing team members and the test expectations contradict the implementation. The onboardingUtils change from && to || also alters routing for every user when onboarding-v3 is enabled. Both need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
Post-signup routing is handled in two places. checkOnboardingRedirect in packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts decides where a logged-in user goes after login. It is called from apps/web/app/page.tsx and the event-types page. Separately, the /onboarding/getting-started server page renders the plan-selection view for anyone who lands on it. Before this PR, the only check for invited users was a client-side redirect, so invited users briefly saw plan selection and payment prompts.

The PR adds a server-side guard to the getting-started page and moves the pending-invite lookup into MembershipRepository as a static method. The lookup that onboardingUtils used to run through raw prisma is now routed through the repository, and the redirect condition in onboardingUtils is changed as well. The intended contract is: a user with an unaccepted membership should be sent to personal onboarding. The current query does not implement that contract.
steps: Entry point: a logged-in user hits / or an event-types page. checkOnboardingRedirect in onboardingUtils.ts decides whether to send them to an onboarding path.

This PR swaps that function's direct prisma.membership.findFirst for MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId, and changes the branch condition from pendingInvite && onboardingV3Enabled to hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled.

Direct navigation to /onboarding/getting-started reaches the server page in getting-started/page.tsx. The PR adds a guard there that calls the same helper and redirects to /onboarding/personal/settings when it returns true.

The helper lives in MembershipRepository.ts as a static method. It is meant to check for memberships with accepted: false. The shipped code filters on accepted: true, which is the inversion that drives most of the findings.
Tests in MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts assert the intended semantics (pending-only → true, accepted-only → false). They will not pass against the current helper.

findings.title: Pending-invite query filters on accepted: true, inverting the check
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, `hasPendingInviteByUserId` (around lines 584-595) filters with `accepted: true`, but the method name and the PR description both say it should detect pending invites, meaning `accepted: false`. Change the filter to `accepted: false`. Then confirm the four cases in `MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts` pass, including the mixed accepted and pending case. Do not change the method signature.

findings.title: onboardingUtils condition changed from && to ||, routing all users when onboarding-v3 is on
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts`, around lines 64-73, the branch that returns `/onboarding/personal/settings` was changed from `pendingInvite && onboardingV3Enabled` to `hasPendingInvite || onboardingV3Enabled`. Restore the `&&` so that only invited users are routed to personal settings when the onboarding-v3 flag is on. Keep the repository-based `hasPendingInvite` lookup. Do not change the fallback return on the next line.

findings.title: Integration tests cannot pass and weaken their own assertions
findings.body:
Beyond the inverted filter, the test file has problems that would hide failures even after that fix.

- The final test uses `expect(result).toBe(team2 ? true : false)`. If no second team exists, the assertion quietly changes what it checks instead of failing or being skipped. Create the second team in the test, or skip explicitly.
- Cleanup runs at the end of each test body, not in `finally` or `afterEach`. If an assertion throws, the user and membership rows leak. Only memberships are cleared in `afterEach`; users are never removed on failure.
- `beforeAll` grabs any existing team with a non-null slug and reuses it. The suite then writes memberships into a real team in whatever database it runs against.
- The mixed-invite test reads `team2` with `findFirst` and may use a team that happens to be unrelated to the test setup.

::code{file="packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts" lines="119-160"}

These tests should create their own users and teams in `beforeAll` and remove everything in `afterAll`, and use fixed assertions.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.integration-test.ts`, rewrite the setup and cleanup. Create dedicated test teams in `beforeAll` instead of reusing an arbitrary existing team. Remove the conditional `expect(result).toBe(team2 ? true : false)` by always creating the second team. Move user and membership cleanup into `afterEach` or `finally` so failing assertions do not leak rows. Keep the four existing cases and their intended expectations.

findings.title: Static helper bypasses the repository's injected Prisma client
findings.body:
The class constructor takes `private readonly prismaClient: PrismaClient = prisma` so callers and tests can supply a client or a transaction. The other methods use `this.prismaClient`. `hasPendingInviteByUserId` is `static` and calls the global `prisma` directly, so it cannot run inside a transaction or use a test client.

This also makes `MembershipRepository.hasPendingInviteByUserId(...)` a different calling convention from `new MembershipRepository(prisma).hasAcceptedMembershipByEmail(...)` in the same file.

::code{file="packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts" lines="584-586"}

Make it an instance method that uses `this.prismaClient`. Update callers to construct the repository with `new MembershipRepository(prisma)`, as the existing `FeaturesRepository` usage in onboardingUtils does.
findings.fixPrompt: In `packages/features/membership/repositories/MembershipRepository.ts`, `hasPendingInviteByUserId` (around line 584) is `static` and uses the global `prisma`. Make it an instance method that uses `this.prismaClient`, matching the other methods in the class. Update the callers in `packages/features/auth/lib/onboardingUtils.ts` (line ~67) and `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx` (line ~30) to construct `new MembershipRepository(prisma)` and call the method on that instance. Keep the boolean return type.

findings.title: Unrelated formatting churn mixed into the functional change
findings.body:
The diff includes changes unrelated to the fix. These make review harder and some break the project's Prettier style:

- `page.tsx` line 35 uses single quotes (`''`) while the rest of the codebase uses double quotes.
- `page.tsx` and `MembershipRepository.ts` reorder imports, and `MembershipRepository.ts` reflows the `hasAcceptedMembershipByEmail` signature.
- `onboardingUtils.ts` reflows the `checkIfFeatureIsEnabledGlobally` call.

Please revert the unrelated formatting so the diff only contains the routing change, the repository helper, and the tests.

findings.fixPrompt: Clean up unrelated formatting in this PR. In `apps/web/app/(use-page-wrapper)/onboarding/getting-started/page.tsx`, change `''` on line ~35 back to double quotes and undo the import reordering. findings.title: Guard uses a clear, early-return pattern that fits the page
findings.body: Doing the invite check at the top of the server page, right after the session check, keeps the redirect server-side so invited users never render the plan-selection view. Reusing the same repository lookup in `checkOnboardingRedirect` avoids two diverging copies of the "has pending invite" logic. Once the filter is fixed, the design is sound.
